intent: The application shell's side panel, anchored to one edge and collapsible off-canvas or to an icon rail, shown as a slide-in sheet on narrow viewports.
typical_uses: The persistent navigation panel of an application shell
A fixed-width side panel that never collapses (`collapsible="none"`)

dont_use_when.situation: A horizontal site navigation with dropdown panels
Switching between panels of one page
A side panel that slides in for one task and is dismissed

invariants.text: Below a 768px viewport, unless `collapsible` is `none`, the panel renders inside a Sheet opened by the provider's mobile state, with a visually hidden title "Sidebar"; the desktop element and its data attributes are not rendered.

With `collapsible="none"` the panel is a plain fixed-width column at every viewport; it ignores the provider's open state and never becomes a sheet. `side` and `variant` have no effect in this mode; the column sits where it is placed among the provider's children.

On desktop, unless `collapsible` is `none`, the outer element carries `data-state` (`expanded` or `collapsed`), `data-variant`, `data-side`, and `data-collapsible`, which holds the `collapsible` value only while collapsed and is empty while expanded.
`className` and every other forwarded prop land on the fixed panel element inside the outer element on desktop, on the sheet's popup on mobile, and on the column itself with `collapsible="none"`.

The panel holds its width in the provider's row where it is placed, so a `side="right"` Sidebar goes after SidebarInset; an inset card then does not apply, because it only follows an earlier inset-variant Sidebar.

The desktop panel is `position: fixed`, so it resolves against the viewport unless an ancestor creates a containing block for fixed descendants (a `transform`, a `filter`, or `contain: layout paint`).

anti_patterns.dont: Mount a Sidebar outside a SidebarProvider
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put it inside SidebarProvider - it reads the provider's state through useSidebar, which throws without one

anti_patterns.dont: Place a Sidebar in a bounded box (a preview frame, a split pane) without a containing block
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the box `contain: layout paint` or a `transform`, or the fixed panel pins itself to the viewport

good.title: A panel collapsing to an icon rail, with its rail

bad.title: Styling expected on the outer element
bad.why: `className` and `data-testid` land on the inner fixed panel, not on the element that carries `data-state`; a selector or query written against the outer element finds neither.
